note: Canonical equipment vocabulary. Every recipe equipment ref must resolve to a key here. Keys with present:false are hard failures, not warnings: a recipe may not be written around gear this kitchen does not have. This file is what makes 'What baking sheet, this wasn't on the list' structurally impossible.

oven.name: oven
oven.notes: Full-size, part of the kitchen stove.

stovetop.name: stovetop
stovetop.notes: INDUCTION, confirmed 2026-08-08. Responds almost instantly with none of the lag a gas or coil burner has. Dial numbers are NOT consistent across burners: some run 1 to 120, some 1 to 10, some low/medium/high.
stovetop.hardRule: Never reference a notch, a number, or 'the lowest setting'. Describe what the pot should be doing and have him adjust to match, then check again in two minutes.

paninipress.name: panini press
paninipress.notes: Two-sided contact heat, cooks both faces at once. Cooks a butterflied chicken breast in roughly half the time of a pan. Treat as a cooking surface, not a sandwich tool.

ricecooker.name: rice cooker
ricecooker.capacity: 6 cups COOKED, 3 cups uncooked. Confirmed 2026-08-11 from the product listing (ASIN B0D1LS87XD), whose own title reads "6 Cup Cooked (3 Cup Uncooked)". 300 W, tempered glass lid, so it can be watched without lifting.
ricecooker.hardRule: NEVER convert a rice cooker measurement into US cups. Measure rice with the cooker's own cup and set water by the pot's own line: N cupfuls of rice, water to the N line. The two were designed as a pair, so the millilitres never need to be known and no arithmetic reaches the cook. Converting is what caused the 2026-08-11 confusion at the stove, described under `history`.

measuringCup.marks: Carries TWO extra scales that are not part of measuring rice: 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 40, 80, 120, 160. Tell him to ignore both and fill to the top line. Naming any of those numbers in a recipe step invites him to reconcile scales that do not need reconciling.
measuringCup.note: The product listing states included components as only an inner pot and a rice paddle. That listing is WRONG, or at least incomplete. Trust the appliance in his hand over the listing.

ricecooker.innerPotMarks: Lines 1, 2, 3 beside a water-drop icon. These are water levels for that many cupfuls of rice, and they are the only calibration that matters.
ricecooker.notes: Simple thermostat switch, not digital. Press the lever down to cook, it clicks itself up to warm when the pot passes boiling. No dial to misjudge.
ricecooker.history: Two errors here, both fixed 2026-08-11 and both worth keeping. (1) The model number read ORIC-00BK6C-GB24, taken off the box cover on 08-08. It was never a model number and no search on it returns this appliance. (2) A recipe converted the rice into 1 1/2 US CUPS because the listing implied no measuring cup was included. The cup existed. Standing in front of the cooker mid-cook, he had a cup marked in quarters and in millilitres, a pot marked 1/2/3, and an instruction in US cups, and said: I do not understand how everything is so contradictory. Nothing about the appliance was contradictory. The conversion was.

bakingtray.name: baking tray
bakingtray.notes: The original, plus two KitchenAid 9x13x1 rimmed sheets bought secondhand 2026-08-02. One rocks very slightly on a corner press, which has no practical effect under parchment.
bakingtray.history: Omitted from step 9 of Brown the Beef and Split It on 2026-08-04. He wrote 'What baking sheet this wasn't on the list wtf'. That is why equipment is a declared list now.

pot_ovensafe_lid.name: oven-safe pot with a lid
pot_ovensafe_lid.notes: At least one of the three pots is oven-safe with a lid. Exact capacities never measured. Required by the no-knead bread.

pan_stainless_large.name: large stainless steel pan
pan_stainless_large.notes: Heat empty and dry on medium 2 to 3 min, flick in a few drops of water: hissing and vanishing means NOT ready, a bead rolling like mercury means ready. Then oil, then food. The water test is safe on a dry pan and dangerous in oil.
pan_stainless_large.history: Went unused for weeks because food sticks to it, and so was reported as not existing. A skill gap presenting as an equipment gap.

blender_bullet.name: bullet blender
blender_bullet.notes: Ninja style, ~16 oz. Small-batch high-shear. Enough for blending cottage cheese smooth. Too small for a 620 ml crepe batter.

slicer_multiblade.name: multi-blade slicer
slicer_multiblade.notes: Interchangeable blades swapped by pressing. One blade grates. Covers slicing and shredding.

bowlset.name: prep bowls
bowlset.notes: 8-piece bowl set plus 2 loose bowls bought 2026-08-08. Small and medium prep bowls are now covered for mise-en-place.

pastrymat.name: silicone pastry mat
pastrymat.notes: A marked surface for rolling dough.

strainer.name: fine mesh strainer
strainer.notes: 3pc set. Finer mesh than the colander, so this is the right tool for rinsing rice. Rice grains fall through a colander's holes.

knifesharpener.name: knife sharpener
knifesharpener.notes: Pull-through slot type. Pull only, heel to tip, never saw. Coarse slot sparingly, fine slot to finish, light pressure, rinse the blade after.

whisk.name: hand whisk
whisk.history: Part of a multi-piece utensil set nobody had ever named. The crepe recipe was written around this kitchen not having one. An item missing from KITCHEN.md is not evidence it is missing from the kitchen.

scale_digital.name: digital kitchen scale
scale_digital.notes: Portioning no longer falls back to package fractions.

teatowel.name: tea towel
teatowel.notes: Small. Too small to cover a rising bowl. Use an inverted second bowl instead.

parchment.name: parchment paper
parchment.notes: No, there is no correct side. One face looks glossier because of how it is silicone-coated and calendered, but both faces are coated and either works. Asked 2026-08-02 during Chicken Crust Pizza, step 2.

papertowel.name: paper towel
papertowel.notes: Always in stock. Never put on a shopping list.

freezerbag_large.name: large freezer bag
freezerbag_large.notes: 12-week freezer rated. Use for raw meat portions.

freezerbag_medium.name: medium freezer bag
freezerbag_medium.notes: Use for sauce portions, they lay flatter and thaw faster. Restocked 2026-08-08.

freezerbag_xl.name: extra large freezer bag
freezerbag_xl.notes: Exactly one. Treat as a one-shot, not a supply.

sharpie.name: sharpie
sharpie.notes: For labelling freezer bags with contents and date. Bought specifically because two unlabelled beef bags had to be re-weighed on 2026-08-08.

foodprocessor.name: food processor
foodprocessor.notes: Nothing here can grind raw meat or make large-batch doughs. Shredding and slicing are covered by the multi-blade slicer.

plasticwrap.name: plastic wrap
plasticwrap.notes: Confirmed absent 2026-08-02. A plate or an inverted second bowl covers rising dough.
